name: Floor box outlet
summary: Plan mark for a flush floor box containing power and often data outlets in open-plan floors.
description: A floor box houses socket outlets and frequently data outlets below a hinged lid flush with the finished floor. Plans draw a square around the outlet mark, sometimes with a diagonal or the letters FB, and list the box contents in a schedule because each box can hold several accessory types.

Floor boxes are used in open offices, meeting rooms and lobbies where furniture is away from walls. They require coordination with the floor finish, raised-floor tiles or screed thickness, so the symbol is often cross-referenced to an architectural floor setting-out plan.
The square does not tell you how many outlets the box contains. Read the floor box schedule for power, data and AV contents and the circuit allocation of each power outlet.
readingNotes: The square outline around the outlet is the usual floor indication.
Expect a schedule listing box contents.
drawingChecklist: Reference the floor box schedule entry.
Coordinate setting out with the floor plan grid.
Tag power circuits and data outlet numbers.
distinction: A multiple socket outlet on a wall shows a gang count; a floor box is an enclosure whose contents are scheduled separately.
